executiveSummary: The bundled 2025 municipality, neighborhood, BAG-place and settlement snapshots identify Roerdalen consistently and the deterministic model passes its arithmetic test suite across all ten presets, six checkpoints and eight services. The operational interpretation is nevertheless not decision-ready. Eight single-hazard presets assign the same complete 24-neighborhood ordering even though Roerdalen's mechanisms are strongly place-specific: the German-fed Roer/Rur floodplain, the Vlootbeek-Putbeek-Pepinusbeek system, pluvial/sewer/groundwater interactions, and heath/forest fire in De Meinweg. The river preset is a broad Maas-distance screening, not a Roer hydraulic scenario with upstream German input, downstream Maas boundary condition, floodplain or defence state. A controlled ignition inside the BRT settlement Meinweg and neighborhood Buitengebied Herkenbosch ranked that containing neighborhood only ninth and still carried synthetic spatial evidence. The 2020 Meinweg fire and Herkenbosch evacuation provide important lessons about care residents, phased evacuation, smoke, radio links and German mutual aid, but do not establish present capacity; the 7 April 2025 Vlodrop-Meinweg fire is closed historical context. The model also lacks German road/transit and supply links, local access restrictions, lifeline topology, acute-care routing, dynamic visitors/agriculture/care populations, and a resource/action ledger. Dated 31 August 2026 drought reporting and date-overlapping municipal works are context only, while empty local Waterinfo and NDW results are NoData rather than zero hazard or open roads. Exact service values must remain synthetic/unknown until operator-backed state is supplied. Corrections should fail closed, preserve validity time and provenance, and make first-72-hour actions, resource constraints and uncertainty visible in both the engine and UI.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek, PDOK and Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: GM1669 official 2025 statistics, generalized geography, BAG places and BRT topography
evidenceSources.edition: Wijken en buurten 2025; BAG/BRT bundled editions recorded by the application
supports: The reproduced application context reports code GM1669, name Roerdalen, province Limburg, safety region Limburg-Noord, center [6.046669061698041, 51.13285534376045], 20,836 residents, density 236/km² and 29.7% age 65+, with the center inside the municipality geometry.

It contains 24 neighborhoods in six districts, 9,670 summed households and a rounded neighborhood population sum of 20,845, nine above the municipal total (0.043%); that small mismatch is expected rounding rather than an event-time population register.

All six BAG places—Herkenbosch, Melick, Montfort, Posterholt, Sint Odiliënberg and Vlodrop—have centers inside the boundary; the BRT snapshot adds 20 named settlement features including Meinweg, Rothenbach, Vlodrop-Station and smaller hamlets.

The annual/static and generalized layers do not locate visitors, care residents, seasonal or agricultural workers, livestock, current occupancy, evacuation demand or people already outside the municipality. Missing statistics remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: 2026–2030 agreement, standing high-water guidance and rainwater/sewer adaptation context
supports: The 2026–2030 agreement names climate change, drought, extreme rain, high water, drink-water shortages, cyber threats and prolonged power failure as pressures. It is a policy/programming document, not evidence that measures are complete or that a present incident exists.

The standing high-water page (https://www.roerdalen.nl/hoogwater) describes conditional roles: the municipality can close roads, check sewer pumps, provide sandbags and evacuate; Waterschap Limburg checks defences and can install temporary barriers; the fire service can pump; and the safety region coordinates. It neither reports current activation nor inventories available crews, pumps, barriers or bags.

The rainwater-disconnection page (https://www.roerdalen.nl/subsidie-afkoppelen-regenwater) links heavy rain to basement/street flooding and sewage contamination, and links infiltration/decoupling to sewer relief and drought. These are distinct pluvial, sewer and groundwater pathways that a single flood scalar cannot represent.
High-water guidance asks agricultural operators to move livestock when required, demonstrating a nonresident/agricultural response demand absent from resident-only exposure allocation.

evidenceSources.title: Roer/Rur extreme-rain system analysis and five-year post-2021 review
evidenceSources.edition: FAQ for the post-July-2021 Deltares analysis; review published 13 July 2026
supports: The water board reports six damaging extreme-rain events in the Roer basin within ten years and notes that parts of the floodplain already inundate at roughly 80 m³/s; July 2021 exceeded a one-in-100-year discharge. These are historical/system thresholds, not a current hydrograph.

Its underlying analysis (https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/publish/pages/7376/een_watersysteemanalyse_wat_leren_we_van_het_hoogwater_van_juli_2021_1.pdf) describes a German-fed Roer entering near Vlodrop and passing Herkenbosch, Melick and Sint Odiliënberg, with old meanders/floodplain behavior and downstream interaction with the Maas system.

The analysis says natural, retention and technical measures have location- and discharge-dependent effects; upstream German reservoirs reduced the 2021 peak. A municipality-center distance curve therefore cannot stand in for upstream input, tributary concurrence, floodplain storage, defences or the downstream Maas boundary.

The 13 July 2026 review (https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/actueel/nieuws/2026/veilig-limburg-water-2021-terugkeert/) says faster German and Walloon information exchange improves warning, while major infrastructure can take around 15 years and much remains in planning. Preparedness materials and data exchange are not an all-clear, completed protection level or GM1669 resource guarantee.

evidenceSources.publisher: Waterschap Limburg and public infrastructure datasets
evidenceSources.title: Vlootbeek catchment, project status, dated drought context and local water-asset observations
evidenceSources.edition: Project page and 31 August 2026 drought update; application public-data snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026
supports: The ongoing Vlootbeek project concerns Reigersbroek/Rozendaal and a future naturalized channel plus replacement/automation of a weir to react to short rainfall and retain water during drought; permits/implementation status must not be interpreted as completed protection or a live gate state.

Water-board material identifies the Vlootbeek catchment with the Putbeek, Pepinusbeek and smaller tributaries across Roerdalen and neighboring municipalities. Their local flash/pluvial behavior differs from Roer river flooding and from groundwater drought.

The water board's liveblog (https://www.waterschaplimburg.nl/actueel/nieuws/2026/liveblog-droogte-2026/) was last updated 31 August 2026: despite rain, groundwater remained very low in north/central Limburg and some streams still fell dry locally. This is explicitly a dated snapshot, not proof of the state on 3 September or over a simulated 72-hour horizon.

The reproduced public snapshot clips 92 harmonized water-system points to GM1669—five sewer pumping stations and 87 weirs—but all 92 lack capacity values. Local Waterinfo observations and forecasts are empty. Counts show known infrastructure, not operability, storage, connectivity or current water level; those fields are NoData/Unknown.

evidenceSources.publisher: Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Noord and Nederlands Instituut Publieke Veiligheid
evidenceSources.title: De Meinweg nature-fire risk, 2020 Herkenbosch evacuation evaluation and later closed incident
evidenceSources.edition: 2020 evaluation; standing risk page and cooperation projects; closed incident of 7 April 2025
supports: The 20–23 April 2020 fire burned about 200 hectares in the roughly 1,800-hectare cross-border Meinweg area. The evaluation PDF (https://www.vrln.nl/sites/vrln/files/2022-10/BRW_IFV_Natuurbrand_in_De_Meinweg_en_de_evacuatie_van_Herkenbosch.pdf) records German assistance and the evacuation of Herkenbosch.

Two care locations began evacuating before the whole-village decision; phased zones, smoke/CO concerns, assisted-living ambiguity, nighttime delay, radio-link weakness and Dutch–German coordination/coupling issues are operational lessons. They do not prove present staffing, transport, beds, radio coverage or mutual-aid availability.

The standing nature-fire page (https://www.vrln.nl/natuurbrand) identifies De Meinweg and difficult access/extinguishing during dry and warm conditions. The cross-border projects run through 2027 and concern preparation, training and exercises; plans are not a current dispatch guarantee.

The 7 April 2025 Vlodrop-Meinweg page (https://www.vrln.nl/nieuwsbericht/natuurbrand-vlodrop-meinweg) says the roughly 200-by-200-metre fire was contained and extinguished, followed by mop-up. It documents historical German cooperation and water-well/shuttle use after 2020, but is closed historical context—not a live incident or proof that those resources are currently ready.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat, Gemeente Roerdalen, Stadt Wassenberg and Grenspark Maas-Swalm-Nette
evidenceSources.title: A73/Roertunnel, local dated works and cross-border road/transit access context
evidenceSources.edition: Standing and dated project pages accessed 3 September 2026
supports: The application has five logical Dutch boundary edges: two representations of the same A73 corridor and one each for N274, N570 and N293. It has no internal local-road graph, bridge/ford/tunnel dependency, German edge or rail station; the duplicate A73 records are not additive independent capacity.

Rijkswaterstaat describes the 2.45-km Roertunnel as a monitored A73 constraint where an incident can close one or both tubes; the A73 page notes automatic tunnel closure and a 4.1-m heavy-vehicle limit for the Roer and Swalmen tunnels. These are static rules/capabilities, not current passability.

Rijkswaterstaat's 2026–2032 planning page (https://www.rijkswaterstaat.nl/wegen/projectenoverzicht/a73-groot-onderhoud-tunnel-swalmen-en-roertunnel/planning) places major closure effects in 2031–2032. The municipal notices for Leropperweg (https://www.roerdalen.nl/reparatie-fietssuggestiestrook-leropperweg) and Posterholt WML work (https://www.roerdalen.nl/wml-vervangt-waterleiding-straten-posterholt) overlap 3 September 2026 by date, but lack a live confirmation/exact clock and cannot be generalized beyond their named phases/streets.

Stadt Wassenberg's access page (https://www.wassenberg.de/buerger/unsere-stadt/lage-und-anreise/) connects the German L117 to the Dutch border and B221/A61. The cross-border park page (https://www.naturpark-msn.de/-Grenspark-beleven/Openbaar_vervoer.html) shows separate Dutch and German stops about 1 km from the Rothenbach border and separate journey planners, not a continuous through-transit service.

The application snapshot lists 25 Dutch GTFS stop areas but no station and no German node. Published geometry and timetables do not establish vehicle availability, accessibility, emergency priority, passenger load, live cancellation or border-road passability.

evidenceSources.publisher: WML, Enexis/Netbeheer Nederland, Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur, DUO and Het Waterschapshuis
evidenceSources.title: Drinking-water sources, grid planning and incomplete lifeline/facility register context
evidenceSources.edition: Standing operator pages and application public-data snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: WML says most Roerdalen villages receive water from Heel, based on Maas surface water, while Posterholt and Montfort receive deep groundwater from Pey. This source diversity is material to contamination, drought, power and transport mechanisms but does not reveal local network topology, storage, pressure, generator endurance or current quality/service.

Municipal Enexis material (https://www.roerdalen.nl/enexis-bereidt-verzwaren-stroomnet-in-posterholt-voor) describes reinforcement work and future planning. A single Netbeheer Nederland capacity-map sample links Posterholt to Maasbracht/Enexis and reports congestion/queues and projects no earlier than 2028; it is a planning point, not live spare capacity, outage status or a complete GM1669 feeder graph.

The reproduced snapshots expose 92 water-system points with no capacities, 55 RDI antenna-register records and six DUO primary schools. Antenna permits/fixed links are not radio/telecom coverage, power backup, backhaul health or emergency-call reachability; schools are not automatically shelters.

No authoritative local gas topology, telecom dependency graph, fuel inventory, backup-runtime ledger, potable-water storage, sewer-pump duty state or verified facility capacity is present. Exact modeled service availability/reserve values therefore remain synthetic estimates and must be labeled accordingly.

evidenceSources.publisher: RIVM, KNMI, Rijkswaterstaat Waterinfo and NDW
evidenceSources.title: External acute care and validity-bounded current observation/event feeds
evidenceSources.edition: RIVM acute-care accessibility v1.1 (3 July 2026); application snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026
supports: The RIVM layer has no acute-care facility in GM1669. Laurentius Ziekenhuis Roermond is the nearest listed 24/7 emergency and acute-obstetric facility at about 7.363 km straight-line from the municipality center; this is not an ambulance route, acceptance, travel-time or surge-capacity calculation.

The snapshot has no local KNMI observation station or PM2.5 monitor, no local Waterinfo observation/forecast record, and no national Waterinfo T+72 water level or T+48/T+72 discharge value. These are coverage/horizon NoData, not zero hazard.

The Limburg KNMI warning snapshot used an official-page fallback issued 2 September 2026 21:36Z, retrieved 23:10Z, at level zero with a 48-hour horizon. It cannot provide a scenario-wide 72-hour all-clear. A reviewed magnitude 0.62015 event near Sint Odiliënberg on 12 July 2026 is a historical catalogue event, not current shaking or local ground-motion evidence.

The NDW clip retrieved 3 September 2026 08:44Z from a source published 08:43Z yielded zero usable unrestricted GM1669 records intersecting the horizon. Empty partial coverage means NoData; it cannot override scheduled notices or prove every road, tunnel or border link open.

identity.summary: GM1669 identity, province, safety-region label, center and boundary containment are internally consistent.
notes: Municipality code GM1669 resolves to Roerdalen in Limburg and the application assigns Veiligheidsregio Limburg-Noord.
The representative center and all six BAG-place centers fall inside the bundled generalized boundary.
Edition/provenance remains part of the claim; a generalized administrative polygon is not a parcel- or flood-defence boundary.

geography.summary: Administrative and settlement geometry is usable for overview, but operational hydrology, forest/fuel, defences, German continuation and access geometry are absent.
notes: The Roer/Rur must be represented from the German boundary through Vlodrop, Herkenbosch, Melick and Sint Odiliënberg to its downstream Maas boundary, with floodplain/meanders and defence states.
The Vlootbeek, Putbeek, Pepinusbeek and smaller tributaries need distinct pluvial, channel, sewer and groundwater mechanisms.
De Meinweg requires fuels, ignition, wind/smoke, water points and access; BRT settlement containment alone is insufficient.
German roads, mutual-aid staging, cross-border public transport and supply continuations are missing.

demography.summary: The static 2025 resident baseline is coherent within rounding and exposes an important older-population signal, but is not event-time occupancy.
notes: The base population is 20,836; neighborhood totals differ by only nine residents (0.043%) after rounding.
Age 65+ is 29.7% and one-person households total 3,189, increasing the need to model assisted evacuation and welfare checks without treating age as automatic vulnerability.
Tourists/recreationists in De Meinweg, care occupants, commuters, seasonal/agricultural workers, livestock responsibility and people already away are not in the static resident allocation.

regionalDetail.summary: All 24 neighborhoods and six districts are present, but sparse/null indicators and rounded aggregates cannot justify precise neighborhood vulnerability or service state.
notes: The context reports 36 regional statistic fields, with district-heating and charging-station coverage absent for all 24 neighborhoods and several socioeconomic fields absent in five neighborhoods.
Infrastructure point counts lack capacity and connectivity, and should remain contextual overlays with affectsSimulation=false unless a documented transformation exists.
Unknown and NoData must survive aggregation rather than becoming numeric zero.

settlements.summary: Six official BAG places and 20 BRT settlement features give useful locality labels, including the park/border localities that municipal averages conceal.
notes: The BRT hierarchy includes ten woonkernen plus smaller buurtschappen, deelkernen and gehuchten.
Meinweg, Rothenbach, Vlodrop-Station and other named features are operationally relevant even when they are not separate BAG woonplaatsen.
Settlement labels are not population, facility, wildfire-perimeter or evacuation-zone measurements.

transport.summary: The Dutch boundary-edge/GTFS snapshot omits internal and German continuity, tunnel and bridge dependencies, and validity-bounded restrictions needed for evacuation and supply.
notes: Five logical road edges reduce to four named Dutch corridors because A73 is represented twice; they must not be summed as independent routes.
There is no station, 25 Dutch stop areas, and no German edge or through-transit node despite the Rothenbach/Wassenberg interface.
A73/Roertunnel closure logic and local access through village roads can dominate external acute-care, mutual-aid and supply routes.
Dated Leropperweg and Posterholt notices overlap 3 September only as scheduled context; the empty NDW clip neither confirms nor disproves their exact live state.

emergencyContext.summary: Plans and historical lessons are strong contextual evidence, but no current GM1669 action/resource/capacity ledger supports the model's operational claims.
notes: High-water and nature-fire pages establish roles and preparedness concepts, not activation, quantity, location or arrival time.
The 2020 Herkenbosch evacuation is evidence for care, communications, smoke and cross-border failure modes—not present capability.
The 7 April 2025 Meinweg fire is explicitly closed/historical; the 31 August 2026 drought liveblog is dated; neither may be promoted into live state.
Acute care lies outside GM1669 and lacks routed travel/acceptance/capacity evidence.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All required presets, checkpoints and services execute deterministically; the pass is computational rather than a calibration endorsement.
notes: All ten presets ran at T+0, +6, +12, +24, +48 and +72 with power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
The earthquake zero direct severity and coastal zero direct flooding at T+24 are model outputs, not authoritative local impossibility claims.

numericalInvariants.summary: The focused reproduction and municipality model tests pass boundedness, determinism and zero-intensity neutrality.
notes: The temporary focused GM1669 diagnostic passed one test and all bounded arithmetic assertions; the required MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1669 audit:model command passed two tests.
A zero-intensity compound run at T+24 returned severity 0, affected population 0 and person-hours 0; background pressure remained 0.038053 and must not be described as hazard impact.
Affected values are model estimates/people-equivalents derived from static residents, not observed persons.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Mechanism-specific locality is not credible: eight hazards share one complete neighborhood ordering and a Meinweg ignition does not prioritize its containing neighborhood.
notes: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and canonical wildfire produced the identical 24-neighborhood ranking hash 50eda1f1409f; the common top sequence begins Rothenbach, Melick, Bedrijventerrein Stationsweg, Reewoude and Vlodrop.

A controlled ignition at [6.177, 51.187] lies inside BRT settlement Meinweg and neighborhood BU16690509 Buitengebied Herkenbosch. At T+24 it produced severity 0.361371, fire 0.249873 and smoke 0.550392, yet the containing neighborhood ranked ninth of 24 at hazard 0.404131.

The canonical wildfire showed zero direct fire and smoke 0.233241 at T+24, while the source-targeted run remained labelled synthetic. Neither result incorporates actual fuels, wind, barriers, access or current drought state.

River flooding uses a broad major-river distance screening and synthetic local redistribution rather than Roer hydraulics; pluvial flooding lacks the Vlootbeek/tributary and sewer/groundwater mechanisms.

serviceDependencies.summary: Eight service trajectories are numerically bounded, but most lack local topology, operator state, cross-border dependencies and resource semantics.
notes: At river T+24 the model reports availability power 0.730463, water 0.699742, drainage 0.613795, gas 0.828567, telecom 0.679119, mobility 0.902037, facilities 0.760349 and supply 0.694356; only mobility/supply routes contain the five NWB logical edges.

Power, water, drainage, gas, telecom and facilities have no local network edges in the output. The model therefore cannot represent the distinct WML Heel/Pey sources, sewer pumps, Enexis feeders, telecom backhaul/power, external hospital route or German continuation.
The exact decimals are synthetic model state. Public asset counts, planning capacity and antenna registrations do not validate availability or remaining reserves.

causalTrace.summary: Provenance exists, but unsupported municipality-specific mechanisms and temporal gaps are not carried as structured Unknown/NoData into claims and UI.
notes: Source inspection found no GM1669-specific guard in sim-core or the web app. River output is labelled derived-screening and other local hazard allocation is synthetic, but unsupportedDimensions is empty/absent despite missing hydraulics, fuel, defence and operator state.

Static annual/register, planned/project, current dated-snapshot and live event semantics must remain distinct. Valid-from, observed/issued-at, valid-to/expiry and retrieved-at are required before a record can change model state.

Empty Waterinfo/NDW clips are NoData; expired or unconfirmed road state and operator capacity are Unknown; a closed historical fire must never appear active; a dated drought report must not be silently carried forward.
The UI must expose those labels and evidence time, and suppress false precision rather than treating absence as zero/open/safe.

recovery72h.summary: The 72-hour curves accumulate impacts and deplete reserves, but do not represent concrete warnings, evacuations, closures, mutual aid, replenishment, repair or care routing.
notes: River severity/flood plateau from T+12 onward at 0.202025/0.647033; affected population rises from 2,572 at T+12 to 3,533 at T+24 and 4,002 at T+48/+72, while person-hours rise to 359,703.74 by T+72.

River service availabilities largely plateau after T+24 (facilities fall to 0.646533 at T+48), while T+72 reserves decline to power 17.53, water 14.76, drainage 8.20, gas 15.92, telecom 9.84, mobility 12.56, facilities 13.48 and supply 17.05.

Compound T+72 reports severity 0.450397, pressure 0.547524, 11,963 affected and 800,808.62 person-hours; service availability is unchanged from T+48 while reserves continue to drain, without an explicit action or replenishment cause.

No checkpoint says which authority warns, checks a sewer pump, moves livestock, closes a road, assists a care resident, requests Germany, routes to Laurentius, restores a feeder or replenishes fuel/water, nor whether it succeeded.

findings.summary: The official municipality identity, boundary, regional hierarchy and place containment are coherent.
findings.evidence: E01 reproduces GM1669/Roerdalen/Limburg/Limburg-Noord, a contained center, six districts, 24 neighborhoods and six contained BAG places; the nine-person neighborhood mismatch is only 0.043% rounding.
findings.action: Retain code-based joins and continue surfacing edition, license, retrieval time and generalized-geometry limitations.

findings.summary: Public current layers are contextual/non-causal, but their empty and incomplete results need explicit decision-facing semantics.
findings.evidence: E04/E07/E08 show no local Waterinfo record, no national full 72-hour hydrologic horizon, zero usable local NDW events, 92 water assets without capacity and antenna permits without service state. The KNMI warning fallback covers 48 hours, not the modeled 72.
findings.action: Keep affectsSimulation=false by default and render NoData for uncovered/absent fields, Unknown for unverified operational state, and valid/issued/retrieved/expiry times next to any current claim.

findings.summary: The river preset is not a Roer/Rur flood model and cannot support local inundation or defence decisions.
findings.evidence: E03 documents a German-fed basin, floodplain onset around 80 m³/s in some locations, discharge-dependent upstream storage, floodplain/meanders and a downstream Maas system. The code instead uses a broad major-river distance/envelope curve and synthetic neighborhood redistribution, producing flood 0.647033 at T+12 without a local hydrograph.
findings.action: Require a selected Roer event/hydrograph, German upstream boundary, tributary concurrence, downstream Maas level/backwater condition, terrain/floodplain and verified defence/temporary-barrier state. If any required dimension is absent, set river depth/extent and operational consequences to Unknown/unsupported.

findings.summary: A shared seed-based allocator gives unrelated hazards the same neighborhood priority order.
findings.evidence: The focused run gives eight individual presets the identical complete ranking hash 50eda1f1409f, placing Rothenbach and Melick first regardless of storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber or wildfire mechanism. E03–E05 require different spatial drivers.
findings.action: Replace shared seeded redistribution with mechanism-specific exposure surfaces and add tests that compare expected local ordering for Roer floodplain, Vlootbeek/pluvial catchments, heat-sensitive built areas, infrastructure cyber dependencies and Meinweg fire/smoke.

findings.summary: The wildfire scenario does not reliably localize De Meinweg ignition, spread, smoke, water or access.
findings.evidence: E05 identifies De Meinweg as a difficult-to-access cross-border nature-fire area and the 2020 evacuation as a concrete smoke/care/coordination lesson. A controlled source inside Meinweg/BU16690509 ranked its containing neighborhood only ninth; the canonical run had zero direct fire at T+24. Both lack fuel, wind, barriers, water-point and access evidence.
findings.action: Use a selectable local ignition/perimeter, fuel/moisture and wind/smoke model, German/NL access and water-point constraints, and explicit evacuation zones. Treat the 2020 and closed 2025 incidents as calibration/lessons only, never current readiness.

findings.summary: Pluvial, sewer, tributary and groundwater/drought mechanisms are collapsed into unsupported synthetic severity.
findings.evidence: E02/E04 distinguish street/basement/sewer flooding, infiltration and drought from Vlootbeek-Putbeek-Pepinusbeek channel response and from Roer flooding. The Vlootbeek weir is an ongoing project, five sewer pumps have no capacity/state, Waterinfo is empty and the 31 August drought liveblog is only dated context.
findings.action: Represent rainfall, runoff/catchments, sewer/pump capacity, surface-water level, groundwater deficit and asset/project state separately; require observation/forecast validity and never carry the 31 August drought state automatically into 3–6 September.

findings.summary: German upstream, road, transit, supply and mutual-aid continuations are absent from the operational graph.
findings.evidence: E03 ties warning to German basin information; E05 documents German fire assistance and past interoperability problems; E06 identifies L117/B221/A61 access and a gap between separate Dutch/German transit stops. The output contains only five Dutch logical road edges and no German nodes.
findings.action: Add explicitly non-additive cross-border road, bus, hydrologic-data, supply and emergency-assistance links with jurisdiction, handoff/interoperability, customs/border status where relevant, availability, capacity, travel time, valid time and Unknown fallback.

findings.summary: A73/Roertunnel and village-road constraints are not propagated into evacuation, acute-care, mutual-aid or supply routes.
findings.evidence: E06 shows tunnel closure/vehicle constraints, only four named Dutch corridors after A73 deduplication, and dated Leropperweg/Posterholt works. E08's zero-record NDW snapshot is partial NoData, not proof of open roads.
findings.action: Route every movement over a directed time-valid graph with tunnel/bridge/local-access dependencies, deduplicate physical corridors, ingest confirmed restrictions with expiry, and show no verified route/Unknown when continuity or live status is missing.

findings.summary: Resident-only affected counts omit care evacuation, visitors, agriculture and external acute-care dependencies.
findings.evidence: E01 records 29.7% age 65+ but only static residents. E02 adds livestock actions; E05 records two care-site evacuations and whole-village phasing in 2020; E08 finds no acute-care facility inside GM1669 and places Laurentius about 7.363 km away only by straight line.
findings.action: Create time-varying occupancy cohorts for home-care/care sites, tourists/recreationists, commuters and seasonal/agricultural workers; add assisted-mobility and livestock tasks; route hospital demand with current accessibility, acceptance and surge capacity or report Unknown.

findings.summary: Exact water, drainage, power, gas, telecom and facility availability/reserve values exceed the available evidence.
findings.evidence: E07 distinguishes WML Heel/Maas surface-water and Pey groundwater supplies but supplies no local topology/state; Enexis evidence is planning/congestion context; 92 water points lack capacity and 55 antenna records do not establish coverage or backup. Model network edges exist only for mobility/supply.
findings.action: Until operator data is licensed and validated, label the service curves synthetic planning estimates, suppress false decimal precision and expose Unknown topology/capacity. Add dependency graphs, backup runtime, restoration/replenishment actions and confidence when data becomes available.

findings.summary: The first 72 hours lack an auditable authority–resource–action–outcome timeline.
findings.evidence: River/compound person-hours and reserves evolve, but E02/E03/E05 describe real roles such as warning, barriers, pumps, road closure, evacuation and cross-border coordination that have no modeled actor, quantity, start, duration, dependency, completion or failure. Compound services plateau from T+48 while reserves drain without an explicit cause.
findings.action: At T+0/+6/+12/+24/+48/+72 display selected event, triggers, accountable authority, requested/deployed resources, route, capacity, start/end, success/failure and consequence; keep unavailable facts Unknown and distinguish recommendation from confirmed action.

findings.summary: Storm, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and earthquake presets are deterministic stressors rather than municipality-validated events.
findings.evidence: The coastal preset has no direct flood at T+24 but retains indirect wind/service effects; earthquake direct severity is zero although E08 has one tiny historical reviewed event near Sint Odiliënberg. KNMI's level-zero fallback is 48-hour context only. None provides local heat, ice, wind, cyber dependency or ground-motion calibration.
findings.action: Label these presets synthetic/unsupported by dimension, select mechanism-appropriate authoritative inputs when available, and never translate zero modeled direct impact or an expiring warning into impossibility/all-clear.

corrections.summary: Make Roer/Rur river flooding event-bound and fail closed when upstream German input, downstream Maas boundary, terrain/floodplain, tributaries or defence state is missing.
corrections.validation: Add GM1669 fixtures for at least low/threshold/extreme Roer hydrographs and contrasting Maas boundary/defence states; assert plausible Vlodrop–Herkenbosch–Melick–Sint Odiliënberg/floodplain changes, provenance and Unknown output when any required hydraulic dimension is absent.

corrections.summary: Replace the common seeded neighborhood ranking with mechanism-specific surfaces for Meinweg fire/smoke, Vlootbeek/pluvial/sewer/groundwater and the other presets.
corrections.validation: Assert that the eight unrelated presets no longer share the full GM1669 ordering; a controlled Meinweg ignition must prioritize the containing fuel/access zone unless an explicit barrier/wind model explains otherwise, while each output states spatialEvidence and unsupportedDimensions.

corrections.summary: Build a directed, physical-corridor-aware access graph with German continuation, A73/Roertunnel and local restrictions, cross-border transit/supply/mutual aid, and strict valid-time semantics.
